notes.text: The complete original was viewed once, followed by both existing native halves once each. Every prose line, display, marginal line, deletion, rule, brace, arrow and numbered object was checked against the accepted text and both witnesses. Seven existing crops were reused; no new crop or enlarged half was made.

The page writes the extension and lift diagram, chooses a universal covering object, gives a fundamental-group automorphism identity, then writes another extension, actions on I and J, and two final connector expressions. These are source statements, not assertions independently proved by this audit.

The three findings are local: a possible extra suspension point, raised abbreviation letters, and a qualification of one argument glyph. The deletion states posons and the duplicate (3), the full word structure, the ss-gp abbreviation, the circled/ruled III, and all accepted arrow-versus-bar distinctions are confirmed.

M0662 remains resolved as variations, with medium confidence. Its initial v and the prolonged -tions/-ons ending are visible in the existing rotated crop. No original MARKS decision is changed by this audit.

The existing E/Sigma remaining-doubt entry is retained rather than removed. Its alphabet confidence is low under the current shared notation. Accepted pure-alphabet difference rows 17 and 18 use medium confidence; these should be aligned to low if main updates report metadata. Mixed rows 12 and 16 contain independently secured arrows/accents as well as the alphabet doubt and should not have all evidence weakened indiscriminately.

No source text is proposed for the isolated tiny points above the lower final connector: they do not form a supported label or punctuation in that position. The possible upper-margin fourth point is treated differently because it lies within an explicit continuation sequence, but its paler color is kept as a doubt.
The two pencil pagination numerals are retained without attribution. No other page image, packet or report was inspected in this second-reading assignment.
